Consider the region $D$ shown above. If $R=[-2,2]\times [-1,3],$ and

$$
{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of $f(x,y)?$

- ${\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y, & (x,y)\in R∖D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in D\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}0, & (x,y)\in R∖D \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y, & (x,y)\in D\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y, & (x,y)\in D\cap R \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}$
worked_solution:
First, let's draw our region $D$ and rectangle $R:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065540/assets/e79856c97ab7e4dd27bb1f476fd911c2e7d77aac6ab54fe50597b3aafbca720c.png)

Notice that the rectangle $R$ contains the region $D$ completely. 

Now, if we define $f(x,y)$ to be equal $\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ on $D$ and to be equal $0$ outside $D,$ we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given functions.

- We cannot use function I. This function is not identically zero for all points in $R\,∖D.$ For example, $(x,y)=(2,2)\in R\,∖\,D,$ but the functions are nonzero at this point.

- Functions II and III are equals $\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ on $D$ and equals $0$ outside $D.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
